question: In Goldfinger, Bond's Aston Martin hides a red button inside the top of the gear stick. Press it and an unwanted passenger is gone. What does the button fire?
source_excerpt: The gear lever hid a small red button. Pressing it released a section of the roof and fired the passenger ejector seat.

extra.why_interesting: Nearly everyone has a mental picture of the gadget-packed Bond car. The question lets them pull out the most outrageous gadget, and the gear-stick button detail makes the answer feel like a reward.
extra.verification_notes: In Goldfinger the DB5's gear-knob red button fires the passenger ejector seat; no newer development changes this (https://www.thejamesbonddossier.com/lifestyle/cars/the-gadgets-of-the-db5.htm).

explanation: The ejector seat flings the passenger out through a panel in the roof. It became the most famous single gadget in Bond history, and toy versions of the car sold in the millions.

question: Tourist boats there head for a needle-shaped limestone rock rising out of the sea, which everyone now calls 'James Bond Island' after a villain's lair was filmed there. Which country is it in?
source_excerpt: Khao Phing Kan is an island in Phang Nga Bay, northeast of Phuket. Ko Tapu, a nearby islet, is commonly grouped with it under the 'James Bond Island' name.

extra.why_interesting: Players don't expect a film location to have literally renamed a place on tourist maps. The limestone-pillar and boat-trip footholds let them reason their way to Southeast Asia.
extra.verification_notes: Ko Tapu / Khao Phing Kan ('James Bond Island') in Phang Nga Bay is in Thailand, featured as Scaramanga's lair in The Man with the Golden Gun (https://Www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ko_Tapu).

explanation: It is Khao Phing Kan in Phang Nga Bay, the hideout of Scaramanga in The Man with the Golden Gun. The film's nickname stuck so well that it has largely replaced the real name with visitors.

question: The white Lotus that turns into a submarine in The Spy Who Loved Me was sold at auction for about a million dollars. The buyer, a famous tech entrepreneur, said he wanted to make it transform for real. Who bought it?
source_excerpt: Tesla's Elon Musk Revealed as $649,500 Buyer

extra.why_interesting: A movie prop ending up with a modern tech mogul is an unexpected link between 1970s Bond and today. The 'make it really transform' detail is a fair foothold toward someone known for futuristic vehicles.
extra.verification_notes: Multiple outlets confirm Elon Musk bought the Lotus Esprit submarine at the 2013 RM Auctions sale for roughly $866K–$997K and said he wanted to make it work as a real submarine; no newer event changes the buyer.

explanation: Musk bought the original underwater prop, which had sat forgotten in a storage unit for years before it was rediscovered. He said he was disappointed to learn that it couldn't really drive into the sea.

question: Four actors who all played James Bond: George Lazenby, Timothy Dalton, Pierce Brosnan and Daniel Craig. Which one starred in only a single official Bond film?
source_excerpt: He played James Bond in On Her Majesty's Secret Service (1969)

extra.why_interesting: All four are genuine Bond actors, so nothing on the surface gives it away. Players have to recall that one of them walked away after a single outing, and many will be tempted by Dalton, who also had a short run.
extra.verification_notes: Lazenby is the only one of the four with a single Eon Bond film (On Her Majesty's Secret Service, 1969); Dalton has 2, Brosnan 4, Craig 5; see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Lazenby.

explanation: Lazenby was an Australian model with almost no acting experience. He turned down a multi-film contract after On Her Majesty's Secret Service, while Dalton made two films, Brosnan four and Craig five.
